chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked him about a man who died while owing a debt equal to the value of his shroud. He said: 'What he left is used for the cost of his shroud, unless some people trade on his behalf (using his assets to cover the shroud cost), so they shroud him and the remaining debt is paid from what he left.'
ai.seo_question: How is the cost of burial shroud handled when a deceased person's debt equals the shroud's value?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the priority of burial expenses (*kafan*) over general debts, ensuring the deceased is honored in death even if it consumes the entire estate. The exception of *ittijar* (trading/leasing assets) highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence to preserve the estate's value for creditors while fulfilling the religious duty of dignified burial. This ruling underscores the balance between the rights of the deceased (*haqq al-mayyit*) and the rights of creditors (*haqq al-nas*).
